name: chipmunk-physics
desc: 2D rigid body physics library written in C
why: A compact 2D rigid body physics engine is a real simulation door, though it is a library and more plumbing than spectacle.

brief.what_it_is: Chipmunk2D is a 2D rigid body physics library written in C, aimed at 2D video games. A program builds a simulation space, adds bodies with circle, convex polygon, or beveled line segment shapes, and steps the simulation. What comes out is the updated position and motion of each body, plus collision events, impulse amounts, and query results (nearest point, raycast, shape, and bounding box queries). The README describes it as simple, lightweight, fast and portable, and says it is MIT-licensed. It is a library, not a standalone app; the bundled demo app draws graphics straight from the simulation space.
brief.why_it_exists: The author says the aim is to give 2D developers access to the same quality of physics you find in newer 3D games.
brief.how_it_works: The README describes a bounding box tree with temporal coherence or a spatial hash for broad-phase collision detection, and contact persistence (credited to Erin Catto) for impulse solving. Joints, collision filtering with layers and exclusion groups, sleeping bodies, and a contact graph are also listed. Chipmunk 7 adds ARM NEON optimizations, autogeometry code, and a multithreaded solver.

commands_seen.context: Unix build step from the README: run CMake in the source directory. Builds a dynamic library, a static library, and the demo application, and needs CMake installed.
Unix build step from the README, run after 'cmake .' to compile the libraries and demo.

brief.install_notes: No Homebrew-specific notes were in the README. Build routes listed: on Mac OS X, the included Xcode project, the CMake files, or the xcode/macstatic.command script to build a static lib and package headers. For iPhone, the Xcode project or xcode/iphonestatic.command, which builds a fat library (release for device, debug for simulator) that you copy into your project as the Chipmunk-iOS directory. On UNIX, run cmake then make, which needs CMake and, on Ubuntu, GLUT and libxmu for the demos. On Windows, Visual Studio projects are in msvc/. The C API documentation is in the doc/ directory of the repo. Nothing about accounts or runtimes beyond a C compiler and these build tools.
brief.standout: It is a small, dependency-free C99 engine that the README says has many language bindings, so it is often reached through another language rather than used directly. The author also runs a contracting business around it, which the README advertises openly.
brief.status: Maintained. The latest commit is 2026-01-08 ('update copyright'), the README was last changed 2025-08-14, and the Codeberg page shows 1,475 commits, 18 tags, 11 branches, 44 open issues and 24 open pull requests. The README's 'NEW IN CHIPMUNK 7' section marks Chipmunk 7 as complete. The Codeberg page does not show a latest release date, so the tag history was not checked.
brief.caveats: The README says the MSVC 9 Visual Studio project may not work because the author no longer has MSVC 9, and asks for help fixing it. It also notes build errors on Ubuntu when GLUT or libxmu are missing. The demo drawing routines poke at undocumented or private APIs, so the author says they are not the recommended way to draw Chipmunk objects. The README's contracting pitch is the author's own company. The homepage (Codeberg) needs JavaScript, but the README text loaded fine. The programming guide is mentioned but no direct URL appeared in the README.
